supporting: the fact that input() returns text

claims.claim: When a prompt is supplied, input() writes it to standard output without a trailing newline, reads a line, removes the trailing newline, and returns a string.
input() raises EOFError when it reads end-of-file.
print() converts positional objects to text, separates them with its sep value, and follows them with its end value; the defaults are a space and a newline.
By default, print() writes to sys.stdout, while sys.stdin is used for interactive input and input() prompts use stdout.
The sep, end, file, and flush arguments of print() are keyword arguments; sep and end must be strings or None.
Because input() returns text, a program should make the intended interpretation explicit before using an entered value as a number; the conversion details belong to a separate lesson.
